chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from the one who mentioned it, from Al-Husayn ibn Abi Al-A'ala, who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'May Allah have mercy on a servant who is chaste and self-restraining, and who refrains from begging, for it hastens the disgrace in the world, and the people do not make him self-sufficient in anything.'
He said, 'Then Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) cited a verse of Hatim: "When I recognized despair, I found it to be riches; when the soul recognized it, greed was poverty."'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and social consequence of begging according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links self-restraint (al-ta'affuf) with the avoidance of the humiliation of begging, noting that those who persist in asking are hastened to disgrace in this world because people's charity does not truly suffice them. He illustrates this by quoting Hatim al-Tai, emphasizing that spiritual richness arises from recognizing one's need for God, whereas greed leads to poverty. This hadith is central to the Shia concept of dignified self-sufficiency, distinguishing between necessary need and the vice of habitual begging.
